transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, yeah, thanks for seeing me. Um, I came in because... well, I'm a high school teacher, and I've just been really struggling to get through my work lately. Like, I can sit down with a stack of essays or a curriculum document, fully intending to get it all done. I'll have my coffee, my desk is clear... actually, I just got this new desk from IKEA last weekend. It's one of those adjustable standing desks? I thought maybe standing up would help me work better because sitting all day is supposed to be terrible for your posture anyway. My brother-in-law has one and he swears by it, though he works in tech, so he's always just typing code or whatever. 

Anyway, sorry, what was I saying? Oh, right. So I'll sit—or stand—at the desk with the essays, and within like ten minutes, I realize I’ve just been staring at the exact same page. I'll be thinking about three completely different things, like whether I remembered to switch the laundry or if my car needs an oil change, and I'm barely taking in a single word of what's actually right in front of me.
Did you experience similar difficulties with attention or focus when you were a child or teenager?

Yeah, actually, I did. Even way back in primary school, my report cards always said the exact same things. Like, "bright but careless," or "doesn't finish work unless closely supervised." My parents were constantly finding these crumpled up worksheets at the bottom of my backpack that I just completely forgot to turn in. Which is funny, because now I'm the one handing out the worksheets. I try to make them interesting, you know? Like last week we were doing this unit on the Industrial Revolution, and I found this really cool interactive map online that shows how the factories spread across Europe. The kids actually seemed to like it, well, most of them. There's always a few who just want to play games on their Chromebooks. I mean, I get it, those Chromebooks are pretty distracting. I had to confiscate three of them just on Tuesday. 

But yeah, the focus thing... it's definitely not a new problem for me. It's just always been there, I guess.
Do you often feel physically restless, fidgety, or like you have trouble sitting still for long periods?

Um, not really? I mean, I don't feel like I have to be running around or anything. I can sit still just fine. Well, mostly. I might bounce my leg a bit when I'm grading, but I think everyone does that, right? It's just a habit. Kind of like how I always have to have a pen in my hand when I'm teaching. Not even to write with, just to hold. I lost my favorite pen last week, actually. It was this really nice metal one my sister got me for my birthday. She's always getting me these fancy office supplies because she thinks it'll help me stay organized. She got me this leather planner last year that I used for exactly three days before I lost it in my car. My car is a total mess right now, to be honest. I keep meaning to clean it out, but by the time I get home from school, I'm just so drained. 

But no, to answer your question, I don't really feel physically restless. It's more just... my brain won't stay put, you know?
